To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
virus detection methods for wild plants should be tested and validated to ensure accurate ecological studies of virus dynamics in wild plant communities.

ELISA can be more efficient for detecting BYDV PAV in wild plants than RT PCR; the efficiency of ELISA detection of BYDV PAV is affected by the tissue sampled and by tiller age; RT PCR detection of BYDV-PAV can be improved by using a modified extraction method that includes a step to remove inhibitors; and the efficiency of RT PCR detection of a virus can vary depending on the plant host.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing guidelines to improve the accuracy of virus detection in wild plants, and to ensure that ecological studies of plant viruses in natural ecosystems are not compromised by methodological biases that may lead to inaccurate conclusions about virus dynamics.
